title: Create reusable data-flow diagram for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Context
Enterprise security reviews and RFPs repeatedly request a simple, high-level data-flow diagram that explains how Redwood Inference handles customer prompts/outputs across deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem). Today, Sales/SEs are using ad-hoc sketches in decks and inconsistent language in one-pagers.

This ticket creates a *single, reusable* visual diagram (with small variants) that can be embedded across:
- Security FAQ (Confluence)
- Compliance one-pagers (SOC 2, Data Residency/Retention, Encryption/KMS)
- Public-friendly docs page (redwood-docs) where appropriate

## Goals
- Provide a clear, “security-review-friendly” diagram that explains data flows and boundaries without over-specifying internal architecture.
- Ensure the diagram is consistent with approved claims (no roadmap promises; align to current retention/residency wording).
- Create exports and alt-text so the diagram can be used in Confluence, Drive one-pagers, and redwood-docs.

## Non-goals
- Not a detailed network diagram; no IP ranges, vendor-specific topology, or internal service names.
- Not a compliance claim (e.g., does not assert ISO certification).
- Not a new feature spec.

## Deliverables
1) Figma source file with reusable components
- Component(s) for the three modes:
  - Hosted API
  - Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  - Private (VPC and on-prem)
- Shared iconography + legend (Customer, Redwood Control Plane, Customer VPC, Storage/Logs, Identity Provider)

2) Export set
- SVG (preferred for docs) + PNG (for slides) at 1x/2x
- 16:9 slide-friendly version and 1-pager (A4/Letter) version

3) Text companion
- Short caption + alt-text per deployment mode
- “Notes/footnotes” block with required caveats (e.g., residency depends on region selected; retention varies by configuration/deployment mode; evidence via NDA)

## Content requirements (what the diagram must show)
- Actors/Systems
  - Customer Application (caller)
  - Redwood API Endpoint / Inference Runtime
  - Redwood Console (optional/secondary)
  - Customer Identity Provider (SSO/SAML) as a logical integration point
  - Audit logs (events) and operational logs (errors/metrics) as distinct concepts

- Core data categories (use neutral labels)
  - Request payload (prompt + parameters)
  - Response payload (model output)
  - Metadata (account/project identifiers, timestamps)
  - Audit events (login/admin changes, API key changes, policy changes, etc.)

- Deployment boundary differences
  - Hosted: Redwood-managed environment; customer calls public endpoint; logs stored in Redwood systems.
  - Dedicated: separate dedicated capacity boundary; still Redwood-managed but isolated; show separate “Dedicated Inference Plane” box.
  - Private: customer-managed network boundary (VPC/on-prem); show control plane vs data plane boundary; emphasize that runtime executes within customer boundary.

- Security-control callouts (high-level only)
  - Encryption in transit (TLS)
  - Encryption at rest (managed; KMS options where applicable)
  - Access controls (SSO/RBAC) and audit logging

## Wording / Legal safety rails
- Use “can be configured” only where true today.
- Avoid absolute statements like “no data ever stored” or “data never leaves the EU.” Use qualified phrasing:
  - “Data is processed in the region selected for the deployment, subject to service availability.”
  - “Retention for logs and certain operational data varies by configuration and deployment mode.”
- Do not include specific subprocessor names, cloud providers, or region lists in the diagram itself (those belong in the one-pager text).

## Stakeholders for review
- Security/GRC: Dr. Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov, Daniel Carter
- Product Security PM: Naomi Feldman
- Solutions Engineering: Markus Klein, Colin O'Donnell, Fatima Noor
- Messaging: Camila Reyes, Soojin Lee
- Docs alignment: Elliot Price

## Acceptance criteria
- Approved by Security/GRC + Product Security PM + Marketing reviewer (no redline items).
- Diagram is understandable by a procurement/security audience in <60 seconds.
- Exports are delivered in a shared drive folder with stable links and version tag.
- Alt-text and caption block included for docs/Confluence accessibility.

## Links
- Working outline (Security FAQ refresh): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/security-faq-refresh-outline.json
- Messaging pillars: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/security-and-trust-messaging-pillars.json
- Data retention language alignment: PM-4860
- One-pager template refresh: DES-2911

## Open questions
- For Dedicated: do we depict separate control plane or represent as “Hosted control plane + dedicated data plane”? Pending SE/Security preference.
- For Private on-prem: do we include as a footnote variant or separate small panel? (Goal is to keep to one page.)
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Field feedback is consistent: prospects want a diagram they can paste into their security questionnaire packet. Please keep it minimal and avoid anything that looks like an internal architecture diagram.

2026-01-14 (Camila Reyes): Messaging request: align labels to “Hosted / Dedicated / Private” exactly (avoid “SaaS” / “Self-hosted”). Add a small legend for shared responsibility (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed).

2026-01-16 (Markus Klein): For Dedicated, customers ask whether data is isolated. Diagram should communicate isolation without making hard guarantees about “single tenant” (varies by contract/implementation). Suggest label: “Dedicated capacity (isolated GPU pool)”.

2026-01-20 (Naomi Feldman): Please ensure we separate audit logs from request/response payload storage. We should not imply we store prompts by default. Use neutral “request/response payload is processed” and push retention details into footnote text.

2026-01-23 (Marcus Lin): Security review note: show TLS for in-transit. For at-rest, avoid specifying algorithm; keep to “encrypted at rest” with KMS option callout where applicable. Do not include any vendor logos.
2026-01-27 (Olga Petrov): GRC note: avoid implying ISO certification. If referencing ISO, use “aligned controls” language in accompanying text only. Diagram should not carry compliance badges.
2026-02-03 (Elliot Price): Docs needs: provide an SVG that renders well on the docs site and include alt-text. Avoid very light gray text; it fails contrast in dark mode screenshots and printouts.
2026-02-06 (Daniel Carter): Evidence process reminder: include a footnote like “SOC 2 report available under NDA via evidence request process.” Keep it as a footnote outside the diagram boxes.

2026-02-11 (Talia Benson): Consolidated feedback: 1) keep three panels with consistent layout; 2) add boundary lines for ‘Customer boundary’ vs ‘Redwood-managed’; 3) keep callouts to 3 max (TLS, encryption at rest/KMS, audit logs).
2026-02-18 (Camila Reyes): Final pass: replaced “prompt” with “request payload” and “completion” with “response payload” (more neutral for RFPs). Approved from marketing perspective.

2026-02-21 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Exports and caption/alt-text delivered to the enablement kit folder; owners can embed into one-pagers + FAQ. Follow-up: if PM-4860 changes retention wording, ensure footnote text is updated in the diagram caption block.
